intro: You are at Öküzini Cave, in Antalya province, in the Upper Palaeolithic. Its neighbour is Karain. What makes this cave special is its layers: it is one of the few places where the passage from the end of the ice age to the Neolithic is recorded in an unbroken sequence.
history: The cave lies a kilometre south of Karain. Its layers, between 16,000 and 10,000 BC, document the end of the ice age in Anatolia better than anywhere else. Turkish and French excavations traced, step by step, how hunter-gatherer groups changed their diet and their tools as the climate warmed.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Epipalaeolithic layers, the microlithic tool finds, the incised rock panel and the excavation sections.
facts: Did you know? The name means 'the ox's den', and it comes from the incised figure of a bull on the cave wall. And its layers cover 16,000 to 10,000 BC without a break — the best record in Anatolia of the end of the ice age.
outro: This brings our tour of Öküzini Cave to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This cave has kept its record unbroken for millennia; let it stay that way for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
